notes: rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed ed25519-dalek and sha2 crates. PublicKey and PrivateKey are newtypes over Go's byte slices (a private key is the seed followed by the public key); Go's panics on bad key lengths are errors with Go's messages, and Verify returns Result<bool>. Signing rejects a private key whose public half does not match its seed, where Go signs with whatever half the key carries (deviation mismatched-public-half-rejected). The key types implement crypto::Signer (PrivateKey) and add PKIX/PKCS#8 DER hooks for x509. ed25519-dalek has no Ed25519ctx (a context without prehashing), so Options with a context and no hash return an error. The crate pulls the proc-macro crate curve25519-dalek-derive on x86-64 (ADR 0003).

GenerateKey.note: None is Go's nil reader (crypto/rand.Reader); Go's reader argument becomes `ed25519::generate_key_with_rng`, which takes the reader first; the plain function uses the system source (ADR 0005). Go always honours the reader.

Options.Context.note: Ed25519ph contexts work; Ed25519ctx (context without a hash) is not exposed by ed25519-dalek and the project does not build signature schemes itself (ADR 0003), so signing and verifying with it return an error

PrivateKey.Equal.note: takes &dyn Any in place of crypto.PrivateKey

PrivateKey.Public.note: the crypto::Signer trait method public returns a reference to the same key

PrivateKey.Sign.note: Go signs with whatever public half the 64-byte key carries, even one that does not match the seed (crypto/internal/fips140/ed25519.newPrivateKey). That is the double-public-key hazard: signatures over one message under two public halves can reveal the private key. This crate deliberately rejects a key whose public half does not match its seed (security over parity; AGENTS.md: never weaken a check). Go ignores the reader argument, so there is no rng parameter.

PublicKey.Equal.note: takes &dyn Any in place of crypto.PublicKey

Sign.note: Go signs with whatever public half the 64-byte key carries, even one that does not match the seed (crypto/internal/fips140/ed25519.newPrivateKey). That is the double-public-key hazard: signatures over one message under two public halves can reveal the private key. This crate deliberately rejects a key whose public half does not match its seed (security over parity; AGENTS.md: never weaken a check).

Verify.note: Returns an error where Go panics on a bad public key length.
